title: AI Security Research Should Better Incentivize Defense Research
abstract: arXiv:2605.23448v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: This work examines an imbalance in artificial intelligence (AI) security research: the field tends to produce more work on attacking AI systems than on defending them. Drawing on related academic papers, we find biased attack-to-defense ratios across subfields, including federated learning, speech recognition, membership inference, large language models, etc. The imbalance possibly means far beyond a simple count: attack papers are routinely evaluated under favorable conditions that make threats look more severe than they are in practice, while defenses are held to a stricter standard that few can meet. The result is a literature rich in demonstrated vulnerabilities and thin on usable and deployed protections. We thus argue that AI security research should better incentivize defense research.

translated_title: 人工智能安全研究应更好地激励防御研究
translated_abstract: 这项工作研究了人工智能（AI）安全研究中的一个失衡现象：该领域产出的攻击AI系统的研究往往多于防御AI系统的研究。通过查阅相关学术论文，我们发现多个子领域中都存在偏向攻击的攻防比例失衡，包括联邦学习、语音识别、成员推理、大语言模型等。这种失衡的意义可能远超简单的数量对比：攻击论文通常在有利条件下进行评估，使威胁看起来比实际更为严重，而防御方法则被以更严格的标准来衡量，很少有方法能够满足。其结果是，现有文献中充斥着已被证明的漏洞，而可使用且已实际部署的防护措施却寥寥无几。因此，我们认为AI安全研究应更好地激励防御研究。
tldr: AI安全研究领域存在攻击研究多于防御研究且评估标准不公的失衡现象，本文通过分析多个子领域的攻防论文比例，呼吁学术界更好地激励AI防御研究。
en_tdlr: AI security research overproduces attack studies evaluated under favorable conditions while defenses face stricter standards, and this paper calls for better incentives for defense research across subfields like federated learning and large language models.
